To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the memory half-life for visual information is 3 s, and that the memory for color and luminance information are stored in independent memory channels.

(1) human memory performance for random block patterns is similar for patterns defined by either luminance or color; (2) the memory for luminance- and color-defined patterns decays with time as an exponential function; and (3) the decay function is similar for both luminance- and for color-defined patterns.

the question of whether and to what extent the human visual system is able to store and process color information in a way similar to luminance.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human visual system uses the same mechanisms for storing information in patterns defined by luminances and color contrasts.
the human visual system is not capable of storing both the pattern and color information in a random block display in a single memory trace.
memory for random block-patterns is a function of pattern information, not of color or luminance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
visual memory for random block-patterns is fast, short-lived, and position-dependent, and that the memory system is able to extract both pattern and color information from visual stimuli.
the visual system is able to store both color- and luminance-contrast derived information, and that this information is stored independently of each others.
the memory mechanism for luminance and color defined pattern information is a common, fast and spatially limited one, and that it can be easily overwhelmed by the memory demands of a visual task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the visual system is very efficient in storing information in random block patterns defined in either luminance contrast or color contrast.
the visual system has a very limited ability to store information about random patterns.
visual memory for random block pattern information is very fast and very short lived.
